f: What is tajwid?
b: Giving every letter its right: its point of articulation and qualities, and the rules it takes from the letters around it.

f: What is the ruling on learning the rules of tajwid as a science?
b: Fard kifayah: a communal obligation.

f: What is the ruling on reciting the Qur'an with tajwid?
b: Fard 'ayn on everyone who recites, as far as he is able; Ibn al-Jazari رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says whoever does not recite with tajwid is sinful.

f: What is a 'clear mistake' (lahn jali)?
b: A mistake that changes a letter or a vowel, whether or not it changes the meaning; it is forbidden.

f: What is a 'hidden mistake' (lahn khafi)?
b: A mistake in the finer rules, like missing a ghunnah or the length of a madd; experts notice it.

f: How many points of articulation (makharij) are there in the view of Ibn al-Jazari?
b: Seventeen.

f: What are the five main areas of articulation?
b: The open space of the mouth and throat, the throat, the tongue, the lips, and the nasal passage.

f: Which letters come from the open space (al-jawf)?
b: The three letters of madd: alif, and sakin waw and ya' preceded by a matching vowel.

f: Which letters come from the deepest part of the throat?
b: Hamzah and ha' (ه).

f: Which letters come from the middle of the throat?
b: 'Ayn and ha' (ح).

f: Which letters come from the part of the throat nearest the mouth?
b: Ghayn and kha'.

f: Where is the qaf pronounced from?
b: The back of the tongue, with the soft palate above it.

f: How does kaf differ from qaf in articulation?
b: Kaf is from slightly further forward and lower on the back of the tongue.

f: Which letters come from the middle of the tongue?
b: Jim, shin and ya' (when not a madd letter).

f: Where is dad pronounced from?
b: One or both edges of the tongue against the upper molars.

f: Which letters come from the tip of the tongue with the roots of the upper front teeth?
b: Ta' (ط), dal and ta' (ت).

f: Which letters come from the tip of the tongue with the edges of the upper front teeth?
b: Za' (ظ), dhal and tha'.

f: Where does fa' come from?
b: The inside of the lower lip with the edges of the upper front teeth.

f: Which letters come from the two lips?
b: Ba', mim and waw (when not a madd letter).

f: Where does ghunnah come from?
b: The nasal passage (al-khayshum).

f: What are the letters of the throat (al-huruf al-halqiyyah)?
b: Hamzah, ha' (ه), 'ayn, ha' (ح), ghayn and kha'.

f: What does hams (whispering) mean?
b: The breath runs on when the letter is pronounced.

f: What are the whispered letters?
b: The letters of فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتَ: fa', ha' (ح), tha', ha' (ه), shin, kha', sad, sin, kaf and ta' (ت).

f: What does shiddah (strength) mean?
b: The sound is held back completely when the letter is pronounced with sukun.

f: What are the strong letters?
b: The letters of أَجِدُ قَطُّ بَكَتْ: hamzah, jim, dal, qaf, ta' (ط), ba', kaf and ta' (ت).

f: Which letters are between strong and soft (tawassut)?
b: The letters of لَنْ عُمَرَ: lam, nun, 'ayn, mim and ra'.

f: What does isti'la' (raising) mean?
b: The back of the tongue rises towards the palate, making the letter heavy.

f: What are the raised letters?
b: The seven letters of خَصَّ ضَغْطَ قَظْ: kha', sad, dad, ghayn, ta' (ط), qaf and za' (ظ).

f: What are the closed letters (al-huruf al-mutbaqah)?
b: Sad, dad, ta' (ط) and za' (ظ): the tongue is closed against the palate.

f: What are the whistling letters (al-safir)?
b: Sad, zay and sin.

f: What is qalqalah?
b: An echoing bounce when the letter is sakin.

f: What are the letters of qalqalah?
b: The letters of قُطْبُ جَدِّ: qaf, ta' (ط), ba', jim and dal.

f: When is qalqalah strongest?
b: When stopping on a qalqalah letter that has a shaddah, as in الْحَقُّ.

f: What are the two letters of lin (softness)?
b: Sakin waw and ya' preceded by a fathah, as in خَوْف and بَيْت.

f: Which letters have inhiraf (deviation)?
b: Lam and ra'.

f: Which letter has takrir (repetition), and what should the reciter do with it?
b: Ra'. The reciter should avoid actually repeating it.

f: Which letter has tafashshi (spreading)?
b: Shin.

f: Which letter has istitalah (elongation)?
b: Dad.

f: What are the four rules of nun sakinah and tanwin?
b: Izhar (clarity), idgham (merging), iqlab (conversion) and ikhfa' (concealment).

f: When does nun sakinah or tanwin take izhar?
b: Before the six throat letters: hamzah, ha', 'ayn, ha', ghayn and kha'.

f: What are the letters of idgham for nun sakinah and tanwin?
b: The six letters of يَرْمُلُونَ: ya', ra', mim, lam, waw and nun.

f: Which letters of idgham take ghunnah?
b: The four letters of يَنْمُو: ya', nun, mim and waw.

f: Into which letters is nun merged without ghunnah?
b: Lam and ra'.

f: Why is there no idgham in دُنْيَا, بُنْيَانٌ, قِنْوَانٌ and صِنْوَانِ?
b: Because the nun and the following letter are in one word; it is read with izhar mutlaq.

f: What is iqlab?
b: Changing nun sakinah or tanwin into a hidden mim with ghunnah before ba', as in أَنْبِئْهُم.

f: Before how many letters is nun sakinah or tanwin concealed (ikhfa')?
b: Fifteen: all the remaining letters of the alphabet.

f: How long is a ghunnah held?
b: Two counts.

f: What is the rule of nun and mim with shaddah?
b: Ghunnah held for two counts.

f: What are the three rules of mim sakinah?
b: Ikhfa' shafawi, idgham shafawi and izhar shafawi.

f: When is mim sakinah concealed (ikhfa' shafawi)?
b: Before ba', with ghunnah, as in تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَة.

f: When is mim sakinah merged (idgham shafawi)?
b: Before another mim, with ghunnah.

f: Before which letters must the reciter be most careful to keep mim sakinah clear?
b: Waw and fa', because they are close to it in articulation.

f: When is the lam of 'al-' pronounced clearly (lam qamariyyah)?
b: Before the fourteen letters of ابْغِ حَجَّك وَخَفَّ عَقِيمَهُ.

f: When is the lam of 'al-' merged (lam shamsiyyah)?
b: Before the other fourteen letters, such as ta', tha', dal, ra', sin, shin and nun.

f: When is the lam of the name Allah heavy?
b: After a fathah or a dammah, as in قَالَ اللهُ and عَبْدُ اللهِ.

f: When is the lam of the name Allah light?
b: After a kasrah, as in بِسْمِ اللهِ.

f: When is ra' heavy?
b: When it has a fathah or dammah, or is sakin after a fathah or dammah.

f: When is ra' light?
b: When it has a kasrah, or is sakin after an original kasrah with no raised letter after it in the same word.

f: Why is the ra' in ارْجِعُوا heavy even though it follows a kasrah?
b: Because that kasrah is not original: it belongs to a connecting hamzah.

f: What are the three main kinds of madd in al-Jazariyyah?
b: Necessary (lazim), obligatory (wajib) and permissible (ja'iz).

f: What is natural madd (madd tabi'i)?
b: A madd letter with no hamzah or sukun after it; it is held for two counts.

f: What is madd muttasil, and how long is it held?
b: A madd letter followed by hamzah in the same word, as in جَاءَ; it is obligatory, held four or five counts in Hafs.

f: What is madd munfasil?
b: A madd letter at the end of a word followed by hamzah at the start of the next, as in بِمَا أُنْزِلَ; it is permissible, two, four or five counts.

f: What is madd lazim, and how long is it held?
b: A madd letter followed by a sukun that stays whether joining or stopping, as in الضَّالِّين; six counts.

f: What is madd 'arid li'l-sukun?
b: A madd letter followed by a sukun caused only by stopping, as in الْعَالَمِين when stopping; two, four or six counts.

f: What is madd al-badal?
b: A hamzah followed by a madd letter, as in آمِنُوا; two counts in Hafs.

f: What is madd al-lin?
b: A lin letter followed by a sukun from stopping, as in خَوْف; two, four or six counts.

f: Which are the three kinds of good stopping (waqf)?
b: Complete (tamm), sufficient (kafi) and good (hasan).

f: What is an ugly stop (waqf qabih)?
b: Stopping where the meaning is incomplete or wrong; one only stops there if forced, then starts again from before it.

f: What does Ibn al-Jazari say about obligatory and forbidden stops?
b: There is no stop in the Qur'an that is obligatory or forbidden in itself, unless there is a reason.

f: With what vowel do you begin the connecting hamzah of a verb whose third letter has a dammah?
b: A dammah, as in اُنْظُرْ.

f: With what vowel do you begin the connecting hamzah of a verb whose third letter has a fathah or kasrah?
b: A kasrah, as in اِذْهَبْ and اِضْرِبْ.

f: With what vowel do you begin the hamzah of al- (the definite article)?
b: A fathah.

f: What is rawm when stopping?
b: Pronouncing part of the vowel (about a third) quietly, on a dammah or kasrah.

f: What is ishmam when stopping?
b: Rounding the lips after silencing the last letter, as a sign of a dammah, without sound.

f: Can rawm be used on a fathah?
b: No.

f: How should za' (ظ) and dad be told apart?
b: By their points of articulation and by the istitalah of dad; al-Jazariyyah lists every word in the Qur'an written with za'.

f: Name three things al-Jazariyyah teaches about the written Qur'an.
b: Words written separate or joined, the feminine ta' written open, and how to begin with the connecting hamzah.

f: Who wrote al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah?
b: Imam Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jazari رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 833 AH).

f: Who wrote Tuhfat al-Atfal?
b: Shaykh Sulayman al-Jamzuri رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, a student of tajwid in Egypt (12th century AH).
